threatCard.summary: A critical maritime passage is experiencing significant disruption following a security incident. This has led to vessels diverting their routes or pausing their journeys, and war-risk insurance premiums for cargo in the region have seen a sharp increase. Carriers are temporarily suspending new bookings on the affected lane pending security reviews.

publicSignals.summary: Multiple wire reports describe transit through the Strait of Hormuz disrupted after a maritime security incident; several tankers are holding or rerouting and war-risk insurance premiums on Gulf-routed cargo have jumped sharply.
EIA notes a large share of seaborne crude and LNG transits the Strait of Hormuz; a sustained closure would force long reroutes and lengthen lead times for Gulf-origin energy and chemical inbound.
Shipping desks report a partial closure window at the Strait of Hormuz with carriers pausing bookings on the Gulf lane pending a security review.

playbooks.summary: Coordinate the immediate assessment of high-impact suppliers and initiate communications with internal and external stakeholders regarding the developing situation.
steps: Identify suppliers presenting elevated exposure scores.
Confirm current operational status and inventory availability with the most critical suppliers.
Establish robust internal communication channels for rapid updates and decision-making.
Begin drafting external communication to key affected stakeholders, ensuring transparency and managing expectations.

playbooks.summary: Investigate and secure alternative sourcing options for critical materials and review existing supplier contracts for relevant mitigation clauses.
steps: Identify and pre-qualify alternative suppliers for critical components originating from affected regions.
Review contracts with all exposed suppliers for force majeure, business continuity, and penalty clauses.
Initiate proactive discussions with secondary or alternative suppliers to understand their production capacity and lead times.
Develop comprehensive contingency plans for potential material sourcing shifts, including exploring new supplier relationships.

playbooks.summary: Plan for potential re-routing of inbound shipments and assess current inventory levels to mitigate any immediate supply chain interruptions.
steps: Evaluate all current in-transit shipments originating from the affected Strait of Hormuz region.
Explore and establish viable alternative shipping routes and transportation modes for inbound materials.
Assess existing inventory levels for all critical components sourced from exposed suppliers to determine immediate buffer capacity.
Coordinate with internal warehouses and external logistics partners to optimize current stock deployment and storage.

playbooks.summary: Continuously monitor the evolving geopolitical situation and provide detailed impact assessments across the entire supply chain.
steps: Establish and maintain continuous monitoring of geopolitical developments and maritime conditions in the Strait of Hormuz region.
Quantify potential financial, operational, and reputational impacts of sustained supply disruptions from high-exposure suppliers.
Develop and model various impact scenarios for different levels of disruption severity and duration.
Provide regular, concise updates to the war room on the overall risk posture, emerging threats, and potential future impacts.

recoveryOptions.title: Expedite inbound on the most exposed lanes
recoveryOptions.summary: Move the most exposed inbound to priority/air freight to close the gap between runout and supplier recovery.

recoveryOptions.title: Activate qualified backups for the dual-sourced lanes
recoveryOptions.summary: Switch the lanes that have a qualified backup on file to the alternate supplier while the primary lane is disrupted.

recoveryOptions.title: Reallocate safety stock to the highest-revenue lines
recoveryOptions.summary: Shift available on-hand cover toward the highest-revenue exposed lines to extend runway past the disruption.

recoveryOptions.title: Escalate allocation with the single-source suppliers
recoveryOptions.summary: Escalate to secure allocation from the single-source suppliers that have no qualified alternate to switch to.
